wallpapers.title: THE SUN'S HOT ATMOSPHERE
wallpapers.line1: The Sun's million-degree atmosphere in ultraviolet light: hot gas caught in its tangled magnetic field.
wallpapers.line2: Solar Orbiter, 77 million km from the Sun  ·  9 March 2025  ·  ESA & NASA/Solar Orbiter/EUI Team, E. Kraaikamp (ROB), CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO

wallpapers.title: TOTAL ECLIPSE
wallpapers.line1: The Moon hides the Sun's bright face, so its outer atmosphere, the corona, shows. Seen from Dallas, Texas.
wallpapers.line2: Total solar eclipse  ·  8 April 2024  ·  NASA/Keegan Barber

wallpapers.title: A FLARE AND THE MOON
wallpapers.line1: A flare, a sudden burst of radiation, flashes on the left. On the right, the Moon has just crossed in front of the Sun.

wallpapers.title: ECLIPSE FROM ORION
wallpapers.line1: Behind the Moon, the Artemis II crew saw the Sun hidden for nearly an hour. Venus and Saturn are marked.
wallpapers.line2: Artemis II, camera on an Orion solar array wing  ·  6 April 2026  ·  NASA

wallpapers.title: GIANT SUNSPOT ERUPTS
wallpapers.line1: The biggest sunspot region in 24 years fires a strong flare. Extreme ultraviolet light shows the hot gas.
wallpapers.line2: Solar Dynamics Observatory, region AR 12192, an X3.1 flare  ·  24 October 2014  ·  NASA/GSFC/SDO

wallpapers.title: THE DIAMOND RING
wallpapers.line1: A last bead of sunlight as the Moon makes its final move over the Sun, above Madras, Oregon.
wallpapers.line2: Total solar eclipse  ·  21 August 2017  ·  NASA/Aubrey Gemignani

wallpapers.title: TRANSIT OF VENUS
wallpapers.line1: Venus, the black dot, crosses the face of the Sun. The next time will not come until 2117.
wallpapers.line2: Solar Dynamics Observatory  ·  5 June 2012  ·  NASA/SDO, AIA

wallpapers.title: SPACE STATION CROSSES THE SUN
wallpapers.line1: The Space Station, six people aboard, crosses the Sun at about 8 km a second during a partial eclipse.
wallpapers.line2: Near Banner, Wyoming  ·  21 August 2017  ·  NASA/Joel Kowsky
